prompt: On a number line, what is the **distance** between $-4$ and $7$?
hint: Distance counts the units between two points, so it is never negative. The two numbers here are on opposite sides of zero.

hints.title: 🔁 Another angle
hints.text: Split the trip at zero. Count the units from $-4$ up to $0$, then the units from $0$ on to $7$.
Distance counts the units between two points, so it is never negative. The two numbers here are on opposite sides of zero.
Subtract the smaller number from the larger and take the absolute value: $|7 - (-4)|$. Subtracting $-4$ is the same as adding $4$.

explanation: The distance between two numbers on a number line is the absolute value of their difference.
Set up the difference: $|7 - (-4)|$. Subtracting a negative is the same as adding, so this is $|7 + 4|$.
You can check by counting: $4$ units from $-4$ to $0$ and $7$ more from $0$ to $7$.
Either way the distance between $-4$ and $7$ is $11$ units.
